paragraphs.notes: Continuation of the Markush substituent definition list that runs across several pages; the page opens mid-list with no sentence start and ends mid-list with a trailing comma, and carries no [00NN] paragraph markers (this publication does not use them). The only German prose in it is the repeated connective 'gegebenenfalls substituiertes Mono- oder ...'; everything else is chemical class names, which is why zh and en differ only in those connectives and in German-to-English spelling (Alkinyl -> alkynyl). Printed as-is and not corrected: 'Arylalkinyoxycarbonyloxy', 'Heteroarylalkinyoxycarbonyloxy' and 'Heterocyclylalkinyoxycarbonyloxy' each lack the 'l' that the parallel Cycloalkyl- and Cycloalkenyl- terms on the same page have ('Cycloalkylalkinyloxycarbonyloxy'); 'N-Alkyl-N-arylaminocarbonyl-amino' carries a hyphen before 'amino' that the neighbouring 'N-Alkyl-N-heteroarylaminocarbonylamino' does not. Line-end hyphens in 'Mono- oder' and 'N-Alkyl-N-' are the printed suspended and name hyphens, not line-break hyphenation.
